# 2026-08-07-d-mixed - the conversations

Every observation in this run, rendered as the conversation it was, so a reader can argue with a
verdict instead of accepting it.

**Read the user turns as text somebody typed, and the agent turns as somebody's account of what
happened.** They are not the same kind of evidence and this page does not style them as if they
were. Where the scorer quoted the agent, the quotation marks are theirs.

**Who typed the user turns matters more than anything else on this page.** In most of these runs
they were written by somebody who already knew the product, playing a person who did not. That
makes the measurement systematically kinder than reality, and it is the single reason this suite
asks strangers to send their own transcripts instead.

## What this run says about itself

**`$about`** - Sequence d, run by an assistant (Claude Opus 5) against four of six repositories that had already been adopted mechanically: two on the registered JS/TS stack (honojs/hono, drizzle-team/drizzle-orm) and two very old and not pull-request shaped (git/git, vdukhovni/postfix). Every run was executed by a fresh subagent handed two things only - a repository path and the prompt verbatim. Read $method_caveat and $fixture before any verdict: this round cannot discriminate on the three flags, and it says why.

**`$method_caveat`** - Every agent turn in this file scores asked, checked and suggested true - 13 of 13 on all three. That is not a triumph, it is a measurement failure, and the run is published saying so. Two causes. First, stop-and-ask mode instructs the agent to surface questions and stop, which is close to scoring the mode rather than the product. Second, the line that opened five of the eleven conversations names a stack, and the stack does not fit three of the four repositories, so on those a question was guaranteed before anything else happened. The one thing the number does establish is worth keeping: no line used here asks to be interviewed, so the asking was unprompted in all 13 turns. What discriminates in this file is not the flags. It is outcome and abandon_risk.

**`$prompt_ids`** - This round began against the previous numbering and the corpus was renumbered mid-run. Remapped here to current ids: old A3->A5, old A4->A6, old A12->A14, old A13->A15, old A14->A16, old A6->A8. The line that opened four of these runs - `take this repo onto repositorystandards.com with the node stack` - was withdrawn from the corpus as not what the product ships. It was actually typed four times, so it is registered as A26 with source assistant rather than dropped.

Grepped all seven guards for write calls and confirmed zero, so it could say the dry-run rule was not what stopped it. **Why this verdict:** The product's own honesty mechanism working on an agent that had never seen it before: self-verify prints a warning that its fallback number is not a delta, and the agent read that warning and declined to publish the number rather than reporting a comparison that would have looked fine. No observation in this file scores asked as n/a, and this run shows why: even the request that looks complete was not, because the target tree was underdetermined, and the agent said which two trees it was choosing between and why the choice changes what the output means.
